title: Develop with specifics
summary: Replace vague assertions with purposeful examples, actions, observations and consequences, then explain the significance of the evidence without inventing false precision.

sections.title: Development is not just more words
content: E7.1 gave each paragraph one promise. Development supplies the evidence and explanation needed to fulfil that promise. A long paragraph can remain underdeveloped if it repeats an assertion, while a shorter paragraph can be convincing when each detail performs a clear job.

Compare ‘The plan helped us’ with ‘Assigning a deadline to publicity, supplies, prices and staffing exposed the unconfirmed drinks order before the sale.’ The second sentence names an action and an observable consequence that a reader can test against the paragraph purpose.

sections.title: Climb the specificity ladder
content: Move through four levels: assertion, specific evidence, consequence and significance. Assertion: the method improved organisation. Evidence: the group divided four responsibilities and assigned deadlines. Consequence: the checklist revealed an unconfirmed order. Significance: the large event became a set of visible decisions that could be completed one at a time.

Not every sentence needs all four levels, and the order may vary. Across the paragraph, however, the reader should be able to answer: What exactly happened? What changed because of it? Why does that change support the paragraph promise?

sections.title: Choose details by function
content: A useful example names a representative moment. An action shows what someone did. An observation records a relevant condition or response. A consequence shows what followed. One detail can perform more than one role, but every selected detail must help fulfil the paragraph promise.

For the initial-planning paragraph, the four task areas, assigned deadlines and missing drinks order are purposeful. The orange poster lettering is concrete but not useful because it does not demonstrate how the workload became manageable. Specific does not automatically mean relevant.

sections.title: Explain the so what
content: After important evidence, add an explanation bridge: ‘This mattered because…’, ‘As a result…’, ‘This showed…’ or a natural equivalent. Complete the meaning rather than leaving the connector to do the work. ‘This was useful’ remains vague; ‘This mattered because the unfinished order became visible while there was still time to act’ explains significance.

Link significance at two levels when useful: first explain the local effect in the event, then connect that effect to the composition's controlling insight. The missing order was corrected; more broadly, the method replaced anxious guessing with a clear next action.

sections.title: Use selective narrative detail
content: Narrative detail should influence action, tension, character understanding or the turning point. In the rain paragraph, water nearing an extension lead justifies treating electrical safety as urgent. Describing every cloud, shoe and wall colour would slow the moment without clarifying the decision.

Select one or two observations that make the important change visible, then move to response and consequence. Purposeful selection creates vividness more reliably than a catalogue of sensory description.

sections.title: Be precise without inventing precision
content: Specific evidence must remain honest. Do not invent measurements, quotations, exact timings or outcomes merely to sound authoritative. For a reflective response, use remembered details that you can stand behind; for a clearly signalled plausible scenario, keep the conditional framing visible.

Classify weak development as vague assertion, irrelevant detail, missing consequence, missing significance or false precision. Repair only the missing function: specify the action, replace decorative detail, state what followed, explain why it matters or remove an unsupported number.

sections.title: Make the evidence earn its place
content: Make six decisions about specificity, relevance, consequence, significance, narrative selection and honest precision. Complete the group before viewing feedback.
